relationship: The first draw and replacement rule determine the second-draw sample space, which in turn determines the conditional probability.

learnerLoop.action: Fix the given first draw, apply the replacement rule and select possible second outcomes.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The bag and second sample space rebuild after the first event.
learnerLoop.evidence: Counter states, outcome branches and probability checks show the conditional sample space.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Decide which outcomes remain possible and use them as the conditional denominator.

invariants: Replacement restores the relevant counter before the next draw.
Conditional probability is calculated from outcomes consistent with the given event.
safeAdaptations: Vary bag contents, first-draw conditions and replacement rules.
Change scaffolding while keeping both draw states visibly distinct.
nonGoals: Using the original sample space after the condition changes it.

task.description: Current bag scenario, condition, target colour and replacement rule.

model.description: Physical coloured counters show the bag, drawn counter and whether it is returned.
model.visibility: Present throughout; counter slots change by draw/rule/target phase.

working.description: Drag sequence for first draw, replacement decision and favourable-outcome marking.
working.visibility: Always present; the active drop target is generated for the current phase.

evidence.description: Before/after bag states, drawn-counter status and live favourable/denominator fraction expose the conditional sample space.
evidence.visibility: State labels and live probability update during the drag sequence.

completion.description: Completed conditional sample space and next paired/new scenario action.
completion.visibility: Next action is generated only after all required favourable counters are marked.

controls.description: Physical counter drags and scenario reset.
controls.visibility: Only counters valid for the active phase are draggable.

drawn-counter.description: The specific physical counter drawn under the stated condition.
drawn-counter.domain: One generated red or blue token ID.
drawn-counter.source: Bag counters with data-drag-kind=draw and data-id.

replacement-state.description: Whether that same physical counter is returned to the bag before the target draw.
replacement-state.domain: Return or keep out; no numeric input.
replacement-state.output: #bagState, #bag count and the visible bag contents.

conditional-denominator.description: Number of counters remaining in the bag after applying the rule.
conditional-denominator.source: Current bag token membership after draw/replacement.

favourable-outcomes.description: Physical remaining tokens matching the target colour.
favourable-outcomes.source: Target-stage draggable counters selected from the current bag.

conditional-probability.description: Favourable outcomes divided by the post-rule bag size.
conditional-probability.source: Computed from the current physical token state.

modes.guided: The initial pass highlights the next valid counter/drop and supplies the phase instruction; completion still uses the physical counter sequence.
modes.independent: After the first paired case, the next pass is labelled Independent; the same draw/rule/target mechanics and checks remain active.
modes.replacement-pair: The first scenario is followed by a second pass with the replacement rule changed, then a new generated scenario begins.
modes.support: No None/Some/All selector exists; Guided/Independent is the source's only support distinction.

dependencies: Only a counter matching the condition colour can be drawn; the exact physical token is carried into the rule stage.
The rule stage must return or keep out that token before target marking begins; replacement changes the denominator.
Target marking counts only tokens of the requested colour, and every such remaining token must be marked before completion.
#nextProblem is generated after completion and advances the paired step or generates a new scenario.
implementation.completion: The source phase becomes complete when every target-colour token in targetTokens() is selected after the draw and replacement rule; the live conditional fraction and #nextProblem are then shown.
limitations: Bag counts and token IDs are generated for each scenario (2–4 of each colour, total at most 6), so individual counter selectors are state-dependent.
There is no typed fraction answer; the fraction is computed from physical membership and marking.
